Verified per-site (RFC 0107): `exec_queries` runs the always-executing load through `_toArrayInner` — this relation's `exec_main_query` — which instantiates the records itself (relation.rb:1428). The row retires with `split-load-records-out-of-exec-queries`, which lifts `loadRecords` out of `_toArrayInner` and restores Rails' `instantiate_records(exec_main_query)` composition.

Rails' `preload_associations(records)` derives its spec list inside the method; trails promotes `includes` to an eager JOIN per association rather than all-or-nothing, so the caller passes the specs NOT already promoted as a second argument. Pre-existing shape, surfaced now that the live load path carries the `exec_queries` name.

Verified per-site (RFC 0107): this row is `ActiveRecord::Relation::ExplainProxy#first` (relation.rb:24-26), whose body is the one-line `exec_explain { @relation.first(...) }` it already makes. The extractor keys a row by <tsFile, rubyName>, so the proxy member collides with the homonymous `ActiveRecord::Relation#first` and inherits ITS Rails call set. No trails call can satisfy it; the row retires when the extractor disambiguates nested classes.
